newsitem.title: USA: GM lays off 500 transmission workers due to strike.
newsitem.headline: GM lays off 500 transmission workers due to strike.

text.p: General Motors Corp. said Friday it will lay off 500 transmission workers Monday because of the 38-day-old strike at GM's Pontiac, Mich., pickup truck plant.

Marilynn Rowe, a spokeswoman for GM's Powertrain Division, said the 500 second-shift workers at the Ypsilanti, Mich., transmission plant were told not to report to work Monday because the Pontiac strike has curtailed demand for the transmissions.
"We could continue to build (transmissions) for some period of time, but at some point there just needed to be an adjustment of production," Rowe said.

She declined to say how long the transmission layoff was expected to last. The Ypsilanti plant, located about 30 miles west of Detroit, employs a total of about 5,000 hourly workers and also produces passenger car transmissions.

The Pontiac plant is one of three factories in North America that build GM's popular Chevrolet and GMC full-size pickup trucks. The automaker continuing to produce other transmissions for the trucks at plants in Toledo, Ohio, and Romulus, Mich.
About 5,800 members of United Auto Workers Local 594 struck the Pontiac plant April 22 in an effort to pressure GM to hire about 600 additional workers at the plant to help ease increasing workloads.
GM has resisted, saying it needs to operate its plants more efficiently. Union officials said negotiations aimed at ending the dispute made little progress Friday.

Last weekend, GM settled a seven-week strike at its Oklahoma City car plant by agreeing to hire about 300 new workers. A ratification vote for the new local labor contract was expected to be complete on Saturday.
